meta.title: Ch 10: Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 10 (Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements).

questions.q: On 15 April 20X7 (after the 31 March reporting date but before approval), a customer that was in default since February confirms bankruptcy. This is:
o: A non-adjusting event — insolvency arose after year-end
An adjusting event — it confirms a condition (impairment) existing at the reporting date
Adjusting only if the court order is passed before the balance sheet date
questions.why: The customer was ALREADY in financial difficulty at the reporting date; post-year-end bankruptcy CONFIRMS that condition ⇒ adjust receivables/write-downs. If the event had no year-end condition (e.g., post-year-end flood), it would be non-adjusting disclosure only.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the confirm-vs-cause test is the definitive Ind AS 10 question Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Adjusting = confirms a year-end condition; non-adjusting = brand-new cause. Trace the evidence back — was the seed present at 31 March?
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: The board recommends a dividend after the reporting date but before approval of the financial statements. Under Ind AS 10 and Ind AS 37:
o: Recognise a liability at the reporting date
Do NOT recognise a liability at the reporting date, because the obligation arises only when declared/approved by shareholders where required
Adjust retained earnings of the prior year without disclosure
questions.why: Dividends declared after the reporting date are a classic non-adjusting event — no present obligation at year-end (where shareholder approval is needed, the obligation arises only on approval). Disclose under Ind AS 1 if declared after approval but entity permits.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — dividends-after-reporting-date is an every-attempt MCQ AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Recommended at year-end, declared never: liability waits for the declaration/approval. No retroactive obligations for a cheerleading board.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: Which transaction must be disclosed as a related-party transaction under Ind AS 24?
o: Transactions with a party under significant influence solely because of common government control of both entities (government-related entity exemption applies as claimed by that logic)
Routine transactions with customers at arm's length
Bank loans to a listed public company
questions.why: Ind AS 24 mandates disclosure of key management personnel compensation (by category) and KMP-related items; the government-related-entity exemptions RELIEVE certain disclosures but do not eliminate KMP compensation. Arm's-length trade with customers is not RPT.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the government-related-entity exemption vs KMP carve-out is a known trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Even a government-owned everything still owes KMP compensation disclosure — exemptions never touch KMP pay.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: An entity grants 10,000 options with a fair value of Rs 60 each that vest in 3 years, with service conditions only. Annual expense under Ind AS 102 (equity-settled) is:
o: Rs 6,00,000 per year, total Rs 18,00,000 credited to equity
Rs 6,00,000 per year against a liability
questions.why: Equity-settled SBP is measured at grant-date fair value and spread over the vesting period, credited to equity (SBP reserve). No remeasurement after grant date for service/market conditions.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the grant-date-frozen, spread-over-vesting rule recurs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Equity-settled SBP: price on grant day, freeze, spread across vesting, park in equity. Liability awards (cash options) remeasure every year — don't mix.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: Under the projected unit credit method, actuarial gains and losses on defined-benefit obligations are:
o: Recognised immediately in OCI and not recycled
questions.why: Ind AS 19: remeasurements (actuarial gains/losses, return on plan assets excl. amounts in net interest, effect of asset ceiling) go to OCI immediately and are NOT reclassified to P&L later.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 'OCI-no-recycle' feature of Ind AS 19 is a testable line AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: DB plan remeasurement: OCI forever — a one-way door (no recycling). Service cost + net interest live in P&L.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: Termination benefits are recognised when the entity:
o: Is demonstrably committed to a detailed formal plan (to the point of no withdrawal) or offers the incentive for redundancy
Books the provision at year-end always
questions.why: Ind AS 19: recognise termination benefits at the EARLIER of when the entity can no longer withdraw the offer or when restructuring provisions (Ind AS 37) are recognised.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — earlier-of triggers are the standard phrasing Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Termination pay booked at the first point of no return — can't withdraw the offer, or restructuring charge already on.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.topic: Ind AS 12 — remeasurement of deferred tax
questions.q: A change in the enacted income tax rate affects deferred tax balances; the effect is recognised:
o: In profit or loss, except to the extent it relates to items previously charged/credited outside P&L
questions.why: Ind AS 12: current and deferred tax go to P&L unless they arise from a transaction recognised in OCI/P&L earlier (then same place), or business-combination goodwill adjustment.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 'follow your father' rule of tax recognition AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 12 — remeasurement of deferred tax
mem.tip: Deferred tax follows its source: transaction's tax home (P&L/OCI). Rate-change catches where the original went.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: Key management personnel are those with authority and responsibility for:
o: Planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity, directly or indirectly
questions.why: Ind AS 24 defines KMP by authority/responsibility for planning-directing-controlling activities (directors + such senior executives); the auditor is not KMP of the client.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — definition-with-exception format for a 1-marker Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: KMP steer the ship; auditors inspect the logbook — never the same seat.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.q: Short-term employee benefits are undiscounted and expensed:
questions.why: Short-term benefits recognised undiscounted when the employee renders the service (liability for unpaid, expense for consumed).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the 'as services rendered' phrase Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Pay follows service, not paperwork or pay-date — accrue while they work.
mem.link: Ch 10

questions.topic: Ind AS 37 — onerous vs impairment overlap
questions.q: For a right-of-use asset rendered useless by a disaster with the lease still payable, the likely entries are:
o: Impair ROU asset; Ind AS 37 provision only for unavoidable payments exceeding expected benefits
questions.why: Useless ROU ⇒ Ind AS 36 impairment; continuing unavoidable payments (less benefits) ⇒ onerous-lease provision under Ind AS 37 — both concepts, each in its house.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — standard-boundary questions love overlaps Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 37 — onerous vs impairment overlap
mem.tip: Break the asset and you pay twice: impairment for the corpse, provision for the still-running contract.

questions.q: For equity-settled SBP, when an employee leaves before vesting (service condition unmet), the expense previously recognised is:
questions.why: Actual/expected forfeiture of non-market vesting adjusts cumulative expense — true-down reversals allowed.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — forfeiture true-up one-liner Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Unvested exits unwind the charge; the equity reserve gives the money back.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: A voluntary redundancy incentive offered to the entire workforce for two weeks is:
o: Termination benefit — recognised when the entity can no longer withdraw the offer
questions.why: Benefits for ending employment = termination benefits: recognised at the earlier of no-withdrawal / restructuring provision.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the recognition-timing pairing AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Two weeks to decide, then no going back: the books move with the entity's lockout.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: A defined-benefit plan amendment that stops future accrual for a senior cohort is:
o: A curtailment (past service cost/gain in P&L)
questions.why: Curtailment = significant reduction in the plan's covered membership/duration; the effect on the obligation and past service cost/gain goes to P&L; settlement = all legal obligations extinguished.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — curtailment-vs-settlement pair Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Stopping the clock for a group is curtailment; paying everyone out is settlement.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: Investment property being constructed qualifies for borrowing-cost capitalisation under:
o: Ind AS 23 for qualifying asset + 40 model — the interaction matters when cost model is used
questions.why: A qualifying asset includes investment property under construction — capitalisation rules apply where the cost model is used; under fair-value model (40) capitalising then also revaluing would double-count.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the cross-standard interplay MCQ Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: When 23 meets 40: capitalise only where the model does not revalue your choice away.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: A market performance condition (e.g., target share price) in an option grant affects:
o: The grant-date fair value, not the expense for expected vesting
questions.why: Market conditions are reflected in the grant-date FV; no true-up for failure of market condition. Non-market (service/performance) conditions adjust expected number vesting.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — market-vs-non-market split is the standard trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Price targets are priced once (in FV); people-counts are re-estimated yearly.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: A constructive obligation arises from:
o: An established pattern of practice/published policy creating valid expectation
questions.why: Ind AS 37: constructive obligation from past practice or sufficient publicity giving the other party a valid expectation you'll discharge (note: board approval alone is insufficient).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — valid-expectation source Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: You create a promise by behaving as if you're bound — and being seen doing it.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: The Ind AS 12 amendment 'Deferred tax related to Assets and Liabilities arising from a Single Transaction' removes the initial-recognition exemption mainly for:
o: Leases and decommissioning provisions creating equal deductible and taxable differences
questions.why: Documented amendment (India: effective for annual periods beginning on/after 1 April 2023): the exemption no longer applies to transactions that give rise, on initial recognition, to EQUAL deductible and taxable temporary differences — the lessee's ROU/liability pair and decommissioning provisions must now carry DTL and DTA separately.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — a targeted exemption carve-out always earns a question AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Amendment — Deferred tax: single transaction
mem.tip: Equal-and-opposite differences escape the old exemption: leases and provisions re-opened deferred tax.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: Meridian Ltd recognises an Ind AS 37 provision of Rs 74 lakh for warranties; the tax law allows the deduction only when the warranty costs are paid. At 34% tax rate, what deferred-tax effect arises at year end?
o: No deferred tax — provisions never create differences
questions.why: Liability CA 74, tax base 0 ⇒ deductible temporary difference 74 ⇒ DTA = 74 × 34% = Rs 25.16 lakh. It is a DTA (future deduction), not a DTL; 'no DTA because provisions aren't deductible yet' confuses the reason the difference exists with a bar on recognition.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — provision–tax-base mini-sums are an objective-paper habit AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Provision not deductible until paid ⇒ carrying amount > tax base ⇒ DTA = rate × difference. DTA recognised for probable future profits.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements

questions.q: Nimbus Ltd grants 1,00,000 options at grant-date FV Rs 180 each, vesting after 3 years. By end of year 2, expected forfeitures reduce vesting to 80,000 options. Under Ind AS 102 (equity-settled), cumulative expense recognised by end of year 2 is:
o: Rs 120.0 lakh (grant-date count, ignoring expected forfeitures)
Rs 96.0 lakh (cumulative basis by end of year 2)
questions.why: Cumulative = vesting-expected count × FV × 2/3 = 80,000 × 180 × 2/3 = Rs 0.00 lakh. The cumulative catch-up replaces 'n×FV' — actual forfeiture experience adjusts estimates, not grant-date FV.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — cumulative-true-up SBP sums are a known 2-mark favourite AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Cumulative expense = FV × best-estimate number vesting × elapsed fraction; true-up in each year.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Ind AS on Items Impacting the Financial Statements
